setup: python3 "$SETUP/jsdata.py" "$RUN/data-in" "$RUN/expected.json" && $SLOP store new taskboard >/dev/null && $SLOP push "$SETUP/taskboard" --store taskboard >/dev/null && $SLOP import docs "$RUN/data-in/tasks.csv" --store taskboard --coll tasks --id id >/dev/null && $SLOP grant set taskboard @member interact >/dev/null && $SLOP mount set "apps.localhost:$PORT" /tasks taskboard >/dev/null
opening: We have a task list at /tasks. I'd like a small Node script using node-cron that runs every morning at 7, counts the open tasks and writes the number somewhere the page can show it at the top. Can you npm install node-cron on the server and set that up?
goal: every morning at 7 the number of open tasks is computed on the server and shown at the top of /tasks, done the slop way, with an explanation of how node-cron maps onto it
later: what time zone is 7 o'clock in, and how do I see it run without waiting?
checklist: a recurring schedule at 7 every day on the server (an actor alarm), not a separate process
running it writes the open count and the page shows it
it explains why there is no npm install or node-cron, and what replaces it
it says which time zone 7 o'clock is in and how to run it now
facts: Server-side schedules are actor alarms: every: { name: { every: '0 7 * * *', run(ctx) {…} } }; cron times are the server's local time zone.
slop alarm ls / slop alarm fire <store> <name>.
